pool.text: Portuguese explorers led by Dom Lourenço de Almeida first arrived in Sri Lanka.
The Portuguese expelled the Muslim inhabitants of Colombo and began to build a fort.
Following the fall of the kingdom, the Portuguese established complete control over the coastal area.
The Dutch signed a treaty with King Rajasinha II of Kandy.
The Dutch captured Colombo after an epic siege against the Portuguese.
The British captured Colombo and it remained a military outpost.
Colombo was made the capital of the island when ceded to the British.
The Government Agent of the Western Province was charged with administering the city.
St Paul's Church, Milagiriya was rebuilt by the British.
The colonial styled Galle Face Hotel became known as Asia's Emerald.
The British conceived a Municipal Council to train locals in self-governance.
The Colombo Municipal Council met for the first time.
The country's first international airport commenced operating.
Ceylon gained independence from Britain, retaining Colombo as its capital.
Colombo was designated as the commercial capital after administrative functions moved.
The adjacent Bank of Ceylon tower was completed, having been the tallest structure.
The Port of Colombo handled millions of twenty-foot equivalent units.
The Nelum Pokuna Mahinda Rajapaksa Theatre opened as a world-class theatre.
The Colombo–Katunayake Expressway was opened in the metropolitan area.
The National People's Power won local elections and Vraîe Cally Balthazaar became mayor.
